study.title: AgriJetsonBench: External-Power-Referenced TensorRT Benchmarking of Agricultural Vision Models on Jetson Edge Platforms

segmentation.domain: Crop/weed/background 3-class semantic segmentation (plus complementary crop/weed object detection) as a reproducible training-to-deployment TensorRT benchmark on NVIDIA Jetson edge-GPU platforms (AGX Orin 64GB, Orin Nano Super); locked public CropAndWeed_v1 dataset used as fixed deployment workload; dual-source measurement (external board-input logger + internal telemetry), matched-budget 15 W INT8 vs native 50 W/25 W FP16 views, battery-continuation 100%-to-20% endurance runs, J/inference and compute-normalized energy (J/GMAC)
segmentation.best_model: SegFormer-B0 (transformer-style semantic segmentation): strongest accuracy on CropAndWeed_v1 test - mIoU 0.8049, Dice 0.8854, foreground mIoU 0.7115, crop IoU 0.7665, weed IoU 0.6565 (DeepLabV3+ mIoU 0.7774, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 0.7631, BiSeNetV2 0.7278); 3.71 M params, 14.84 GMACs / 29.67 GFLOPs at 640. Deployment (TensorRT batch 1, 640x640): matched 15W INT8 - Nano Super 47.18 FPS / 0.2808 J-per-inference vs AGX Orin 31.95 / 0.5013; native FP16 - AGX Orin 103.61 FPS / p95 9.441 ms vs Nano Super 67.47 / 15.020 ms with near-tied energy

dataset.name: Locked public CropAndWeed_v1 segmentation dataset (Weed-AI, Steininger et al. 2023) as a fixed deployment workload with frozen class list (0 background, 1 crop, 2 weed): train 5,381 / val 798 / test 1,526 images, 1,526 test masks; locked splits, benchmark-order files, labels and license notes packaged. Detection counterpart CottonWeedDet12_v1 (train 3,972 / val 564 / test 1,112, 1,886 boxes) used only for the detection track. Ground/agricultural-robot imagery, not UAV-captured.
dataset.note: images = sum of locked CropAndWeed_v1 split sizes (5,381 + 798 + 1,526). Benchmark paper contribution is the deployment-measurement protocol and measurement-boundary analysis, not new agronomic data collection. Training on Sapelo2 GPU cluster (Georgia Advanced Computing Resource Center); models exported checkpoint -> ONNX -> TensorRT engines (FP32/FP16/INT8, INT8 calibrated on 256 images); resolution ablation at 640 for segmentation (SegFormer-B0 and RT-DETR-R18 stayed at 640; BiSeNetV2 Smin 448).

segmentation.backbone: Four segmentation backbones trained from scratch on CropAndWeed_v1: SegFormer-B0 (hierarchical MiT-B0 transformer encoder + lightweight MLP decoder, 3.71 M params, 14.84 GMACs), DeepLabV3+ (heavier CNN, 40.32 M params, 108.37 GMACs), MobileNetV3-LRASPP (3.21 M, 3.25 GMACs), BiSeNetV2 (3.33 M, 19.23 GMACs); all exported to ONNX and TensorRT at FP32/FP16/INT8 (INT8 with per-size calibration caches and FP16 fallback where needed by the builder), pure engine-level batch-1 timing at 640x640

mIoU.quote: SegFormer-B0 achieved the strongest predictive performance, with test mIoU of 0.8049, test Dice of 0.8854, and foreground mIoU of 0.7115
mIoU.ambiguity: Held-out CropAndWeed_v1 test set. Best of four segmentation models: DeepLabV3+ mIoU 0.7774, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 0.7631, BiSeNetV2 0.7278. Per-class IoU for SegFormer-B0: crop 0.7665, weed 0.6565 (also reported for all segmentation models in Table 4). Foreground (crop+weed) mIoU 0.7115.

mPA.ambiguity: Mean pixel accuracy not reported; mIoU, class IoU, Dice and foreground mIoU reported instead.

F1.ambiguity: F1 not reported; the segmentation accuracy metric is Dice (recorded in the Dice field).

Dice.quote: SegFormer-B0 achieved the strongest predictive performance, with test mIoU of 0.8049, test Dice of 0.8854
Dice.ambiguity: Test Dice on CropAndWeed_v1 (SegFormer-B0). Dataset-wise Dice: DeepLabV3+ 0.8664, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 0.8560, BiSeNetV2 0.8291.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Weed-class F1 not reported; weed-class IoU reported instead (SegFormer-B0 weed IoU 0.6565 - best, vs DeepLabV3+ 0.6230, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 0.5986, BiSeNetV2 0.5457).

crop_F1.ambiguity: Crop-class F1 not reported; crop-class IoU reported instead (SegFormer-B0 crop IoU 0.7665 - best, vs DeepLabV3+ 0.7179, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 0.7009, BiSeNetV2 0.6486).

edge.device: NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin 64GB Developer Kit and NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super Developer Kit - real edge-GPU deployments; TensorRT engines, batch 1, 640x640; external INA260 board-input power logger + internal Jetson telemetry; matched-budget (15 W vs 15 W) and native (50 W vs 25 W) views; main segmentation energy tests on SegFormer-B0
edge.precision: FP16 and INT8 (TensorRT; INT8 with calibration caches, FP16 fallback where required); FP32 reference
edge.framework: PyTorch training -> ONNX export -> NVIDIA TensorRT engines; JetPack/L4T, CUDA, TensorRT versions and nvpmodel clock policies recorded in metadata; pure-engine timing boundary (excludes I/O, preprocessing, postprocessing, NMS, mask decode)

fps.quote: Nano processed 756,122 inferences over 4.452 h at 47.18 FPS
fps.ambiguity: SegFormer-B0 INT8 at 15 W on Orin Nano Super (battery continuation, 100%-to-20% power bank). Matched-budget AGX Orin: 31.95 FPS (1.48x advantage for Nano). Native FP16 (AGX 50 W / Nano 25 W): AGX 103.61 FPS vs Nano 67.47 FPS; AGX locked-640 INT8 best-config median throughput also higher. edge.reported=true.

latency_ms.quote: Median latency decreased from 29.523 ms on AGX to 21.514 ms on Nano, and p95 latency decreased from 29.566 ms to 21.582 ms
latency_ms.ambiguity: PURE TensorRT engine MEDIAN latency, SegFormer-B0 INT8 15 W on Orin Nano Super (batch 1, 640x640); p95 21.582 ms. Matched AGX Orin median 29.523 ms. Native SegFormer-B0 FP16: AGX median 9.420 ms / p95 9.441 ms; Nano median 14.842 / p95 15.020. AGX locked-640 INT8 seg rows: SegFormer-B0 median 7.029 ms (different power mode), DeepLabV3+ 8.353 ms, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 3.975 ms, BiSeNetV2 7.573 ms.

power_w.quote: Nano Super 15 W SegFormer-B0 INT8 ... Avg W 13.15
power_w.ambiguity: MEASURED average external board-input power (INA260 inline logger) for SegFormer-B0 INT8 15 W battery run on Orin Nano Super. Matched AGX Orin avg 16.01 W. Native FP16: AGX 33.20 W (50 W mode), Nano 21.79 W (25 W mode). Idle baselines: AGX 10.920/11.299 W (15/50 W), Nano 5.308/5.663 W (15/25 W). J/inference for SegFormer-B0 INT8: AGX 0.5013 vs Nano 0.2808 (-44.0%).

params_M.quote: SegFormer-B0 had only 3.71 M parameters, but required 14.84 GMACs
params_M.ambiguity: SegFormer-B0 (best segmentation model) at 640; other segmentation models: DeepLabV3+ 40.32 M, BiSeNetV2 3.33 M, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 3.21 M. Detection contrasts: YOLO11n 2.63 M, YOLO11s 9.46 M, RT-DETR-R18 20.02 M.

gflops.quote: SegFormer-B0 Segmentation 3.71 M 1.48e10 MACs at 640 14.84 GMACs 29.67 GFLOPs equiv.
gflops.ambiguity: GFLOPs-equivalent under the paper convention 1 MAC = 2 FLOPs at 640x640 input (14.84 GMACs). Other segmentation models: DeepLabV3+ 216.74, MobileNetV3-LRASPP 6.50, BiSeNetV2 38.47 GFLOPs-equiv.

issues: edge.reported=true: real on-device Jetson measurements with externally referenced board-input power logging. SegFormer-B0 INT8 15 W matched-budget: Nano Super 47.18 FPS / median 21.514 ms / 0.2808 J per inference vs AGX Orin 31.95 / 29.523 ms / 0.5013 J. Native FP16: AGX 103.61 FPS / 9.420 ms vs Nano 67.47 / 14.842 ms. INT8 accuracy retention checked (mIoU/Dice drop <= 0.05, crop/weed IoU drop <= 0.10 vs FP16) - all four main INT8 engines passed.

Benchmark paper: accuracy measured OFFLINE on the locked public CropAndWeed_v1 dataset (ground/robotic sugar-beet imagery, uav_collected=false); the study is a deployment-measurement protocol contribution, not agronomic data collection.

six models/families in the segmentation track; the detection track (YOLO11n/s, RT-DETR-R18 on CottonWeedDet12_v1) is out of scope for the semantic RQ1 record but its deployment evidence (e.g. Nano YOLO11s INT8 145.82 FPS / 0.0767 J vs AGX 80.90 / 0.1814) is cross-referenced.

Dual-source power: external INA260 logger primary; pooled internal-minus-external bias -1.988 W (MAE 2.402 W, RMSE 2.720 W, r 0.970 over 76,691 paired 1 Hz samples) motivates the external-boundary reporting.

Key message: board choice depends on workload, precision, power mode and measurement boundary, not board class alone (Nano wins matched-budget INT8; AGX wins native FP16 high load with near-tied J/inference).
